titleText.es: Por supuesto, el análisis completo es mucho más complicado, pero no puedo quedarme a hablar de eso porque tengo una cita.
titleText.en: The full analysis is of course much more complicated, but I can't stay to talk about it because I have a date.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In statistics, the mediana is the value in the middle after the values have been put in order. It is not necessarily the same as the average.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: aged; no separate English word before an age
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De can introduce a person's age or the numerical value of an age measure. English often turns de plus the number into “aged ...” or simply states the number without a separate word for de.

example.es: Es una persona de veinte años.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Fondo more often means “bottom,” “background,” or “fund.” As a figurative use influenced by English, it can also refer to a pool of available people.

example.es: La empresa eligió entre un fondo amplio de candidatos.
example.en: The company chose from a large pool of candidates.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Solteros is the masculine or mixed-group plural of soltero. With no following noun, it stands for the people themselves.

example.es: Hay muchos solteros en el grupo.
example.en: There are many single people in the group.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; presents the thing as changing
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With verbs such as reducir and ampliar, se lets Spanish describe a change without naming anyone who causes it. English often uses a simple verb such as “shrinks” or “widens.”
Reduce is a present form of reducir used with one thing. With se, it describes that thing becoming smaller.

example.es: El ruido se reduce por la noche.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: I am left; I end up (with me)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Quedo is the present speaker form of quedar. In me quedo sin, it helps say that the speaker is left without something or runs out of it.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins en verdad
cardDefinitions.noteEn: En combines with verdad to form an expression meaning “actually,” “really,” or “in truth.”

cardDefinitions.answerEn: actually; really (as part of en verdad)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Verdad by itself means “truth.” With en, it forms the reusable expression en verdad.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: more; an extra intensifier before mayores here
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Mayor already means “older,” so neutral standard Spanish normally needs only mayores. Más mayor is sometimes heard when distinguishing degrees within adulthood, but it can sound redundant; this use simply emphasizes the older part of the group.

example.es: Mi hermana es mayor que yo.
example.en: My sister is older than me.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Mayor means “older” when comparing age; mayores is its plural form. The same form is used for a masculine, feminine, or mixed plural group.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to become; to get (speaking to one familiar person)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hacerte joins hacer, the unchanged dictionary form, to te, the short word for the familiar person addressed. With an adjective after it, hacerse can mean “to become.”
When it describes age, mayor means “older.” It has the same singular form for a man, woman, or thing.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: marriageable; considered old enough to marry (feminine)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Casadera is the feminine singular form of casadero. The word can sound traditional or old-fashioned because it describes someone in terms of suitability for marriage.
Amplía is a present form of ampliar used with one thing. With se, it says that the thing becomes wider.

example.es: La zona se amplía cada año.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish can leave out a masculine noun that is already understood and keep el before the words that distinguish it. English often supplies “the one.”
Repulsión literally means “repulsion” or strong disgust. A humorous label can extend it to socially creepy or repulsive behavior.

example.en: She felt disgust at the smell.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Novios can mean boyfriends, a dating couple, or romantic partners depending on context.

example.es: Invitaron a sus novios a la fiesta.
example.en: They invited their partners to the party.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins por encima de
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Por, encima, and de work together to mean “above,” “over,” or “more than.”

example.es: Está por encima de la puerta.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: above; over (as part of por encima de)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Encima refers to an upper position, but por encima de is the complete expression used before the reference point.

example.es: La lámpara está por encima de la mesa.
example.en: The lamp is above the table.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; completes por encima de
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De is required before the point, object, or limit that something is above.

example.es: La cifra está por encima de cien.
example.en: The figure is above one hundred.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: end; part of fin de semana, “weekend”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Fin literally means “end.” In the fixed expression fin de semana, the three words together name the weekend.

example.es: El fin de semana fue tranquilo.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; links fin and semana in “weekend”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De remains between fin or fines and semana in the fixed expression for “weekend” or “weekends.”
After a time expression, pasado or pasada identifies the immediately previous one. It matches the expression: el mes pasado, la semana pasada.
Hice is the completed-past form of hacer for the speaker.
Análisis has the same written form in the singular and plural; the surrounding article or verb shows the number.
Crece is a present form of crecer used with one person or thing.
With edad, mediana names the middle stage of adult life. This is different from the statistical mediana, the middle value in ordered data.

example.es: Llegó a la mediana edad con energía.
example.en: He reached middle age full of energy.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks that “you” are the person who worries
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Preocuparse is used with me, te, se, nos, or os. Te is the form for one familiar person addressed as tú.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: worry (special form after no in a command)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Preocupes is the form used when telling one familiar person not to worry. The positive command is preocúpate, but the negative pattern is no te preocupes.
Dice is a present form of decir used with one person or thing. A report, text, or analysis can be the thing that “says” or indicates information.

example.es: El informe dice que todo está bien.
example.en: The report says that everything is fine.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Noviazgo is the period or relationship in which people are a romantic couple before marriage.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; helps pasarse mean “to spend time”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pasarse in the sense of spending a stretch of time uses a matching short word: me, te, se, nos, or os. Se is the form used with one third person.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: spends (a period of time, with se)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pasa is a present form of pasar. In se pasa plus a time period, it describes how someone spends that time.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: ends; part of fines de semana, “weekends”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Fines is the plural of fin. In fines de semana, only fin becomes plural; semana stays singular inside the established expression.
Haciendo is the -iendo action form of hacer. It can name an activity happening during the time described.

example.es: Pasó la tarde haciendo una mesa.
example.en: He spent the afternoon making a table.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Campana normally means a bell. A roughly bell-shaped statistical curve is also called a campana in Spanish.

example.es: La curva tiene forma de campana.
example.en: The curve has a bell shape.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: De can join an invention, theorem, or named object to the person whose name it bears. English may instead use an adjective based on that name.
Carl Friedrich Gauss was a German mathematician. His name appears in terms connected with the normal distribution and its bell-shaped curve.

example.es: La campana de Gauss tiene dos colas.
example.en: The Gaussian bell curve has two tails.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Chica can mean a girl or young woman. Mi chica often means “my girlfriend,” but context can also use it loosely for the woman who would be right for someone.

example.en: He met a friendly young woman.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone runs out of something or is left without it?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of quedarse, then sin, then the missing thing.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Quedarse is the unchanged dictionary form. The short word and the quedar part both match the person: me quedo, te quedas, se queda, nos quedamos. Sin stays unchanged and introduces what is no longer available.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What expression can mean “actually,” “really,” or “in truth”?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The two words work together to confirm something, correct an impression, or emphasize that it is true. The natural English choice depends on that conversational purpose.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone gets older or grows up?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of hacerse followed by mayor.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hacerse is the unchanged dictionary form. The short word and hacer change with the person: me hago mayor, te haces mayor, se hace mayor. Mayor stays singular for one person and becomes mayores for more than one.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce a rough amount or an approximate example with “something like”?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use algo como before the estimate or example.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Algo normally means “something,” and como means “like.” Together they signal that the following amount, description, or example is approximate rather than exact.

example.en: It will cost something like twenty euros.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is above a place or over a limit?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use por encima de before the place, amount, or limit used as the reference point.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Por, encima, and de form one expression. De is required before the reference point even though English “above” or “over” needs no matching word there.

example.es: La temperatura está por encima de treinta grados.
example.en: The temperature is above thirty degrees.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: fin de semana / fines de semana
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use fin de semana for one weekend and fines de semana for more than one.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The expression literally contains “end of week,” but it functions as the ordinary unit “weekend.” In the plural, fin changes to fines while semana remains singular: los fines de semana.

example.es: Visitamos a Ana los fines de semana.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What expression names the middle stage of adult life?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use la mediana edad for “middle age.”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is an established life-stage expression. It differs from la mediana de las edades, which would refer to the statistical middle value of a set of ages.

example.es: Cambió de profesión en la mediana edad.
example.en: She changed careers in middle age.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: orden negativa de tú: no + verbo
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you tell one friend or familiar person not to do something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put no before the verb's special negative-command form. If the verb uses te, put te between no and the verb.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: For a regular -ar verb, the negative form usually ends in -es: hablar becomes no hables. Regular -er and -ir verbs usually end in -as: comer becomes no comas. A short word such as te goes before this negative form, as in no te levantes.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone spends a stretch of time doing an activity?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching short word and a form of pasar, name the time period, then add the activity in its -ando or -iendo form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The short word and pasar change with the person: me paso, te pasas, se pasa, nos pasamos. The final activity form describes what fills the time; it commonly ends in -ando or -iendo, as in leyendo, “reading.”

example.es: Lucía se pasa la tarde leyendo.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: regla de la mitad de la edad más siete
cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is the informal “half your age plus seven” dating rule?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: It claims that half a person's age plus seven is the youngest partner age that would not seem socially inappropriate.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is a folk rule and a common joke device, not an ethical or scientific standard. It can be treated as a numerical boundary when discussing possible partners.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is a campana de Gauss?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: It is a bell-shaped curve representing a normal distribution: values near the center are common and values in the tails are rare.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Gauss is the mathematician whose name is attached to this model. Referring to a point at the extreme of the bell invokes one of the curve's rare tails.

applications.explanationEn: Fin, de, and semana form the established singular time unit; pasado separately identifies which one.
Algo de supplies an unspecified amount, and análisis names the broad activity being quantified.
The fixed expression introduces a correction to the preceding assumption.
Mediana and edad form the established name for this stage of adult life, distinct from the earlier statistical use.
The two words work together as the connector introducing a result.
No begins the negative instruction, te comes before the verb, and preocupes is the special familiar negative-command form.
